cap_confirmation: Resolved opponent levels equal cap+offset-2 at cap 36: Hariyama L34 (36+0-2), Avalugg L35 (36+1-2), Toedscruel L34 (36+0-2), Sawsbuck L35 (36+1-2).

attempts.notes: Togekiss' 2x Air Slash carried the fight, removing Hariyama and Sawsbuck. Avalugg was killed with non-super-effective Dark Pulse specifically so Weakness Policy could never fire. Lost Mega Blastoise to a Muscle Band Body Slam after Horn Leech had chipped it.

strategy_checks.check: Hariyama's Flame Orb self-burn turns on Guts
strategy_checks.evidence: End of turn 1: 'The opposing Hariyama was burned!'; it then used Close Combat from behind Guts on turn 2. The burn is self-inflicted and the Attack drop is inverted exactly as authored.

strategy_checks.check: Hariyama's Facade doubles behind the burn
strategy_checks.evidence: Hariyama got two actions (Fake Out, Close Combat) and died on turn 2 before Facade came up. Close Combat into the Mega was the higher-damage choice on that board, so this is not a miss.

strategy_checks.check: Hariyama opens with Fake Out on an interruptible threat
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1, Fake Out targeted Mega Blastoise - the member that had just Mega-evolved and the biggest threat on my side - and the flinch denied its Water Pulse. Correct target out of two.

strategy_checks.check: Avalugg's Weakness Policy activates on a super-effective hit for the Avalanche retaliation role
strategy_checks.evidence: I killed Avalugg with Dark Pulse (1x) rather than Aura Sphere (2x) precisely to deny the Policy. Two Mega Launcher Dark Pulses did 114 and 30 through its base-46 Special Defense. This is the crack working as documented, not an AI failure, but it does show the retaliation role is opt-in for the player: a special attacker with a neutral move simply never gives Avalugg its turn.

strategy_checks.check: Avalugg's Sturdy survives an OHKO from full
strategy_checks.evidence: No single hit took it from full to zero; the first Dark Pulse left it at 30.

strategy_checks.check: Avalugg's Avalanche retaliates after being hit
strategy_checks.evidence: Avalanche on turns 1, 2 and 3, all into Togekiss at 2x, for 54 and 25. It used the move it was built for.

strategy_checks.check: Toedscruel's Mycelium Might makes status moves resolve last
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 4: Toedscruel's Spore resolved after Sawsbuck's Body Slam, after Togekiss' Air Slash and after Sawsbuck had already fainted - dead last in the turn despite base 100 Speed. That is Mycelium Might's documented drawback, correctly applied.

strategy_checks.check: Spore lands despite the target's ability
strategy_checks.evidence: Togekiss fell asleep for 2 turns ('sleep:2' in the decoded status), which is the Mycelium Might ability-ignoring upside.

strategy_checks.check: Sawsbuck's Serene Grace doubles Body Slam's paralysis chance
strategy_checks.evidence: Body Slam KOed Mega Blastoise outright on turn 4, so no paralysis roll was visible. Sawsbuck's two actions (Horn Leech at 2x into the Water-type, then Body Slam) were both correct targeting.

level_changes.reason: Won on attempt 1 with a single faint. Hariyama is tied for the weakest offset and died to two Air Slashes having landed one Fake Out and one Close Combat.
Tied weakest offset; it got one Spore off and then died to a single 4x Icicle Crash from full HP. Avalugg and Sawsbuck both already sit at +1 and both did real work, so neither moves.

level_change_verification: NOT RERUN - prebuilt ROM, no level override, no make. Needs the main agent's rebuild.
could_this_be_cooler: This is the most coherent regular-trainer team in the block - four distinct, readable mechanics and no dead sets, and the AI played all four correctly. The one structural note: Avalugg's Weakness Policy is a trap that a thinking player declines for free, because Avalugg's Special Defense is so low that any neutral special move kills it faster than a super-effective one would. Suggestion, not applied: the retaliation role would actually threaten if Avalugg's partner could force the super-effective hit - a Toedscruel that leads beside it and Spores the special attacker, leaving only the physical Fighting/Rock/Steel answers on the field, would make the Policy a real decision instead of a button the player never presses.
authored_set_legality: No legality problems. Guts, Sturdy, Mycelium Might and Serene Grace all behaved as printed, and Sawsbuck resolved as SAWSBUCK_SPRING.
notes: No opponent Protect was used in this battle, so the Protect ledger is empty.
